questions.question: OP-01/O52 (failure phases): D79 amends D46 only. So D35 still says a whole read surfaces 'everything', D46's open-call list still holds a closed stream's ValueError, and D46's check says the open and read lists overlap 'only in what any backend request can meet', though both also hold the caller errors and a cancellation. How should the phase lists be fixed?

options.label: One phase table (Recommended)
options.description: A table, D34's categories × whole read / stream open / stream read / close, replaces the prose lists in D35, D45, D46 and D79 (amended to cite it); D46's check is corrected. AX-11's normative form is that table; the prose lists have drifted twice. Source: axes.md AX-11, O52.
options.preview:
| Category (D34) | Whole read | Open | Stream read | close |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| key refused | yes | yes | — | — |
| not found, not an item | yes | yes | — | — |
| permission denied, auth failed | yes | yes | yes | — |
| not readable | yes | yes | yes | — |
| unavailable, timeout | yes | yes | yes | — |
| changed | — | — | yes | — |
| base category | yes | yes | yes | — |
| memory/descriptors as raised | yes | yes | yes | — |
| decode under strict | text form | — | — | — |
| caller error | yes | yes | yes | — |
| closed stream ValueError | — | — | yes | — |
| cancellation | yes | yes | yes | yes |

options.label: Amend lists in place
options.description: D35's whole-read sentence reads as D79; D46's list drops the closed-stream ValueError; D46's check names the caller errors and a cancellation. Three prose lists stay, each correct.

options.label: D46 only
options.description: D46's list and check corrected; D35's 'everything' sentence left, read through D79, so D35 alone still misleads a reader.

questions.question: OP-01/O53 (waiting bound): D59 says a whole read's or an open's waiting is at most the attempt limit times the bound plus backoff. But D73 leaves the number of requests to NP2, and T_idle never fires on a trickle (one byte every 59 s). What bounds that waiting, and what is NP1's scope?

options.label: Per wait, no total (Recommended)
options.description: T_connect bounds each connect, T_idle each wait for the next byte, D38's limit each request's attempts. No figure bounds a call's total waiting or duration; each wait ends, so D12's 'returns or fails' holds. D59's check amended; NP1's scope reads 'D12 bounds each wait, not total waiting or duration'. Source: botocore read_timeout (per socket read); D12's 'a progressing transfer never fails by its size'.

options.label: Add a minimum rate
options.description: A configurable low-speed limit fails a request slower than R bytes/s over T as timeout, so a trickle fails. New store configuration; amends D12 and D13. Source: curl CURLOPT_LOW_SPEED_LIMIT/TIME. A slow but healthy link then fails by its speed.

questions.question: OP-01/O55 (closed-stream retry): D60's row 'caller error | repeats it: a function of the arguments' also covers a closed stream's ValueError (D34, D53). A new OP-01 call opens a new stream, which does not repeat it. How does the caller-level retry table treat it?

options.label: Own row (Recommended)
options.description: D60's table gains 'a read on a closed stream | a new call opens a new stream, which does not meet it'; the caller-error row reads 'caller error, other than a closed stream'. Every D34 row keeps a retry row. Source: O55, D15, D60.

options.label: Outside the table
options.description: D38's caller-level table is declared to cover failures of an OP-01 call or a stream read from the store or its arguments; a closed stream's ValueError is misuse of a released object and gets no row. One fewer row, one more scope sentence.

questions.question: OP-01/O60 (E4 vs E12): on Local or SFTP, O3 truncates a file mid-read, so the read yields fewer bytes than its size at open. D26 and D48 return that as content ('may end short without failing'); D28 says a short body (E12) is never returned as content. Which governs?

options.label: E4 governs (Recommended)
options.description: E12 is a transfer short of the length the backend announced for that transfer, or failing an integrity check. On file-system backends a read that ends short of the size at open is E4's (D26, D48), never unavailable. Source: POSIX read(2) returns 0 at the file's current end; D26.

options.label: Detect it
options.description: A file-system read ending short of the size at open fails unavailable. It is the best-effort detection D26 rejected: a truncate-then-append to the same length is missed, so still no promise, at one stat per open.

options.label: Cite D93's list (Recommended)
options.description: D18's column reads 'a data read (D93's list)': read, read1, readinto, readline, line iteration, chunks are enumerated in D93 only. One place to keep in step. Source: O58, D93, CLAUDE.md principle 4 (single source).

options.label: Add read1
options.description: D18's column enumerates read1 too. Two enumerations, D18's and D93's, to keep in step.

questions.question: OP-01/O58 (async non-I/O methods): D69 makes tell, readable and seekable plain methods on the async stream, a sentence no dialog asked (its option read 'Same methods, awaited'); seek, truncate and write are in neither of D69's lists. Which async stream methods are coroutines?

options.label: I/O awaited, rest plain (Recommended)
options.description: Coroutines: read, read1, readinto, readline, close; async iteration and chunks are async iterators. Plain: tell, readable, seekable, and seek, truncate, write, which raise io.UnsupportedOperation at the call. They make no request. Source: asyncio.StreamReader keeps at_eof plain; D69.

options.label: Every method awaited
options.description: All methods are coroutines, as D69's option text reads: 'await s.tell()'. One uniform rule; aiofiles does this because it runs every call in a thread. Costs an await for answers that make no request.

questions.question: OP-01/O59 (E16 exposure): D62 exposes E16 (O3 metadata-only change) 'at s3 only, through a resume', while D22's dialog has a stream make a new request on 'connection recycled or resume', and D47, D61 and D86 name any new backend request. Through which requests does E16 reach a stream?

options.label: Any new request (Recommended)
options.description: E16 is exposed at s3 through any new backend request the stream makes (a resume, a recycled connection, a prefetch), as D86 reads for E18. Source: D22, D47, D61, D86, NP2 (request count and prefetch not promised).

options.label: Resume only
options.description: A promise that a stream makes a new request only to resume after a dropped connection. It constrains implementations (no ranged prefetch), against NP2's 'prefetch' row.

Which sessions does O46 name?

options.label: OP-03 to 05, OP-10 to 15 (Recommended)
options.description: Every entry whose operation replaces, deletes or moves an item: O6's list (OP-03 to OP-05, OP-12 to OP-15) plus the deletes OP-10 and OP-11. Source: catalogue rows, D65, O6.

options.label: By rule, no list
options.description: O46 names 'every entry whose operation replaces, deletes or moves an item'; each session judges itself in. Nothing to keep in step, but no session is named.

options.label: As is
options.description: O46 keeps its four entries; OP-05, OP-11 and OP-13 to OP-15 learn of the deviation only from O6 or OP-01's spec.

questions.question: OP-01/O61 (formal-model list): D68 says D4 and D9 cite KEY-001, KEY-013, TREE-001 and TREE-002; D9 also cites KEY-002, KEY-004, KEY-005, and D53 rests on KEY-008, all tagged in KeyModel.lean. The Session's reopen line says only the TREE-001 and KEY-013 clauses were read. What is done?

options.label: Complete the list (Recommended)
options.description: D68's list reads D4, D9 and D53 citing KEY-001, KEY-002, KEY-004, KEY-005, KEY-008, KEY-013, TREE-001, TREE-002; the Session's reopen line stays true as what that reopen read. Spec 052's Tested against: KeyModel.lean 'restates the sections ... no bridge makes it govern', so reading it adds no ground.

options.label: Complete and read
options.description: As (a), and this session reads the KEY-002, KEY-004, KEY-005 and KEY-008 clauses of KeyModel.lean, the Session gaining that reading and a finding.

questions.question: OP-01/O62 (log fidelity): beyond D75's two, D41's dialog option ended 'a test that asserts one is a defect', missing from D41's Recommendation, and D43's dialog option read '(S3-compatible endpoints)' and 'an unnamed non-AWS endpoint gets the deviations (eventual, no pinned resume)', which D43's option (a) dropped. No word-by-word sweep ran. What is done?

options.label: Restore, no sweep (Recommended)
options.description: Both texts restored, quoted from O62. No sweep: the decision log is outside this session's ground, and /observe-review's readers compared every decision with its dialog claim by claim. Source: O62, D75.

options.description: Both restored, and an open item asks the next /observe-review for a word-by-word sweep of every option against the log; it blocks the freeze until run.

options.label: As is
options.description: Neither restored; the dialog log stays the only place with the full option texts.
